title: The Empty Side of the Hut

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager's hut-mate has moved out, leaving half the hut bare: move into the space, or leave it for now.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (hutmate), who shared (subject)'s hut, has moved to a new one across the clearing. (hutmate.He/she) is fine. (hutmate.He/she) waves every morning. But the other half of the hut is suddenly empty: a bare patch of floor where a mat used to be, a peg with nothing hanging on it. (subject) keeps walking around the space instead of through it.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) drags (subject.his/her) own mat into the middle of the floor and spreads (subject.his/her) things out a little. Baskets on both pegs. The water jar where the other mat used to be. It feels strange for a few nights and then it doesn't. Sometimes (subject.he/she) still walks around the bare patch out of habit, even though it isn't bare anymore.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) leaves the empty side empty. It isn't a shrine. (subject.He/she) just isn't ready to decide what goes there. A few weeks later (subject.he/she) catches (subject.him/her)self putting a basket on the empty peg without thinking. (subject.He/she) looks at it, decides that's fine, and leaves it there.
